samples.question: This picture shows a mitten-drying room on a plain white background. Two identical dark grey wooden racks, drawn as open rectangular frames, stand far apart: one near the left edge and one near the right edge. Each rack hangs between two and five mittens, all drawn as the same shape at the same size, so mittens differ only in their single flat colour; the thumb of a mitten may point either way, and that never matters. No rack ever hangs two mittens of the same colour. Some mittens may also lie loose on the floor in the empty space between the two racks; a loose mitten is not on a rack and must be ignored completely. Call a colour shared when at least one mitten of that colour hangs on the left rack and at least one mitten of that colour hangs on the right rack. The two racks need not hang the same number of mittens, and the two racks need not be at the same height. How many colours are shared between the two racks? Answer with exactly one of: 0, 1, 2, 3.
